{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study compares preclinical cardiac electrophysiology data (in vitro and in vivo) with clinical QT interval prolongation and torsade de pointes for 100 drugs, providing quantitative measures of agreement and predictive value. It explicitly states it aims to determine the relative value of preclinical data for predicting clinical risk.",
  "arm": "safety-pharmacology",
  "arm_evidence": "Objective: To attempt to determine the relative value of preclinical cardiac electrophysiology data (in vitro and in vivo) for predicting risk of torsade de pointes (TdP) in clinical use.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cardiovascular"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study focuses on cardiac electrophysiology, QT interval prolongation, and torsade de pointes, all of which are cardiovascular endpoints.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The study compares data from multiple drugs, evaluating various preclinical tests (hERG, APD90, QT in dogs) against clinical outcomes, rather than focusing on a single model type.",
  "species": [
    "dog"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "Data on effects on QTc in animals (lowest published values for doses associated with 10–20% QTc prolongation in beagle dogs, or other species if dog data were unavailable).",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study compares preclinical electrophysiology data (hERG IC50, APD90, QT prolongation in dogs) with clinical outcomes (QT prolongation, TdP reports, plasma concentrations), encompassing both biomarker-like measures and hard clinical outcomes."
}
